column3: Conjecture 19; Walnut automata could certify excluded exponents, but the primary reports memory exhaustion. Finite prefixes cannot bound all factors or periods.
Precise lower bound entails the half-area packing problem; diagonal equality gives only an upper construction. Special mountain/permutation configurations do not cover arbitrary point sets.
Lemma 6.2 gives the coclique-extension lower bound and Conjecture 6.3 asks for its converse. Need a uniform eventual upper bound on orders, not a bounded eigenvalue search.

Conjecture 4.2 needs exclusion of every 31,35,...,91 fertility across arbitrary permutation lengths. Theorem 3.5 reduces each fixed fertility to finite length at most f+1, but enumerating S_92 is not cheap; valid-hook structure needed.

Conjecture 4.3 is an asymptotic all-fertility bound; Theorem 3.5 is linear and multiplicative closure alone does not handle large prime fertility values. No uniform sublinear construction established.

Primary distinguishes powered adjacency from edge-indexed nonbacktracking algorithms. Literal mixes incident edges with vertex eigenvectors and does not specify rounding r'd or disconnected diameter; no discovery credit for those formulation defects.

Conjecture 1.5 extends a two-colour density theorem to all k. Merging colours loses the minimum class inequalities; extremal H_m^k construction shows the target scale is sharp but supplies no universal upper bound.

Primary concerns cyclic Z/(2^n) with projective cubes and a specified layer construction, not the vector-space cube problem. Powers-of-two d and layer unions are prior partial cases; arbitrary subsets need a compression preserving cube-freeness.
Conjecture 2.9 uses alternating local weight sums for arbitrary saturated fusion systems and compatible cocycles. Block-realizable/O.W.C. bridge is conditional and cannot settle exotic systems.

Conjecture 1 requires square-free levels and sufficiently large even weight; general orbit count contains the level-one Maeda obstruction. Unconditional simple-Hecke-module bounds are much smaller than the proposed polynomial order.

Retrieved primary prints nbar(t,3)=t+7 as Conjecture 1, contradicting literal claim that it is solved. The every-n tope statement needs both universal and extremal directions; do not retire it solely on the database prose.

Conjecture 1.2 asks for c=2 universally. Theorem 1.3 proves it outside DLO reducts and strictly stable structures; stable cases remain a genuine scope obstruction to using that theorem as a complete bridge.

Conjecture 14 seeks max-min edge separation in no-hole bijective labeling. Bipartition ordering supplies one inequality; proving the converse requires a forced small-gap edge for every bijection. A bipartition bound alone does not prove this.

Conjecture 1.5 needs a strictly better-than-3/4 exponent for every fixed forbidden H. Square-root degeneracy only reaches 3/4; Appendix B conditional improvement is not an unconditional result for arbitrary H.
Conjecture 1.13 includes both perfectness and equality structure for all t. The proved t=3 and disjoint-union results do not force a clique in every extremal longer-cycle-free hypergraph.

Primary defines m(k,a) with b=k, whereas literal temporarily leaves b unindexed. With corrected b=k, Conjecture 3 needs exponential residual multiplicity against every (k-1)-cover; product-type subexponential evidence does not prove that uniform rate.

Conjecture 7.2 extends Theorem 4.4 beyond divisibility or sufficiently large k. Cremona/reduction Lemmas 2.2 and 2.4 are a concrete route, but must uniformly control all exceptional (n,k) and general-position configurations; no such case certificate supplied here.
Conjecture 3.1 is all finite Coxeter types. Type A sl2 operators, dihedral arguments and rank<=4 computer checks leave unbounded B/D ranks; tensor products do not supply irreducible-type operators.

Source Theorem 3.2 proves fmax<=2^((1/2-c)mu) for even-order groups with 2^r=o(n). Take cyclic G_j=Z/(2^j), so r=1, 2=o(2^j); omit finitely many small j. This is a complete existential bridge with increasing orders and one fixed c>0; Section 3 supplies its container/link-graph proof.

Conjecture 5.2(a-c) asks three exact threshold recurrences for all n. Appending 1 proves <= only. Finite partition enumeration could refute an equality, but proving lower thresholds for unbounded n needs a structural classification of collisions.
Conjecture 1.1 quantifies all fixed-step nilmanifolds and every diverging H. Theorem 1.2 handles s=1 at polynomial interval lengths, not slowly growing H or all s. No short full-scope analytic route.

Conjecture 1.1 is every graph with delta>=5. Random regular and large-girth domination algorithms omit low-girth and irregular graphs; exact small domination searches do not prove the universal 4n/11 bound.

Conjecture 5.9 includes exact 276 plateau and all later dimensions. Primary supplies small-dimension SDP bounds and eventual Neumaier theorem but explicitly notes a limitation of its relaxation. No full middle-range certificate.

Conjecture 6.3(a,b) has arbitrary reduced complete intersections. Corollary 6.10 covers quadratic degrees d=1,c-1,c only; Proposition 6.9 equates the remaining part to CB10, not proves it. Complete-intersection length alone cannot control all hypersurface intersections.

Primary f is an extremal minimum class-size parameter for partial colourings; literal calls it maximum size of a colour class. Under the literal non-surjective convention one colour trivially wins. Source Conjecture 2.5 needs all-colour balance; no credit for reinterpreting f.

Conjecture 11.1.5.1 requires Comp(C) to satisfy all associative n-category structure axioms with coherent choices. Low-dimensional examples are not a uniform construction for arbitrary n; contractibility is a substantive missing bridge.

Primary endnote reports a stronger confirmation and points to arXiv:2003.14361. Successor Theorem 12 is list-capable, but displayed Theorem 5 uses ordinary colouring and its partition reduction; full all-f list bridge not audited. Do not promote or assert complete retirement from the endnote alone.

Literal ordinary matching is false: all 2n+1 spokes in the prism P(2n+1,1) form a perfect matching, exceeding n+1 for n>=4. Source Section 8 discusses switching-isomorphism representatives immediately before Conjecture 8.2; this wording correction is uncredited, not a solution of the intended signed-graph problem.

Primary final conjecture requires exact minimal eventual recurrence order for every r, not merely an annihilator. Matrix characteristic polynomials give upper orders; nonzero projections and eigenvalue multiplicities are needed uniformly for lower orders.

Without a binary alphabet, w=abcd has no nonempty even palindrome across either cut, contradicting n/2=2. Source Section 2 is binary in context and Proposition 8 counts zeros/ones; arbitrary-alphabet transcription does not refute the intended binary Conjecture 7.

Conjecture 5 asks an example at every ribbon genus with a strict separation from minimum-genus ribbon bands. Existing lower bounds simultaneously bound band number and fusion number, so they do not create the required gap.

Even-genus Conjecture 1.7 requires both exact spectral infimum and non-attainment. Handle collapse can produce one inequality; reverse inequality and equality-case compactness do not follow from numerical eigenvalues.

Conjecture 1 concerns every principal-minor log distribution at fixed condition number. Diagonal sharpness of one bound does not majorize arbitrary log-minors; k=1 bounded-variable variance is insufficient for k>1.

Source explicitly calls the conjecture vague: sufficiently well-behaved is not a mathematical class. Theorem 5 already proves uniformly recurrent binary uniform-morphic case. A broader classification needs a precise domain and cannot earn credit by selecting the proved subclass.

C0 and C1 in literal are arbitrary constants satisfying one-sided intervals and can be shrunk/enlarged independently. Intended Conjecture 5.5 concerns sharp transition thresholds. Corrected problem needs connectivity control throughout parameter space, not this constant-choice defect.

Conjecture 3.25 is arbitrary marked vinyl graph. Depth 0/1 and selected strand base points are proved cases; moving arbitrary base points requires a graded-dimension/invariance bridge absent from low-depth examples.

Literal omits delta(F)>=1; without that, spanning-tree T-joins prove it for every connected graph (also successor Theorem 1). Intended positive-degree statement is publicly false: Lu-Yang-Zhang arXiv:2009.12802 Corollary 5 subdivides a 3-connected cubic F of even order p, glues K_p at each subdivision vertex, and violates Theorem 2 with T=V(F), defect -p/2<=-2. Successor proof body read; no new credit.

Upper DNF compression must dominate pointwise while preserving width, size independent of n. Standard approximation and lower compression fail the pointwise upper direction; sunflower improvements alone are not a complete bridge to this exponential-in-width target.
Higher-rank Lehmer includes k=1 ordinary Lehmer-type lower bounds. Exterior wedge bounds and special field cases do not remove the unrestricted degree/discriminant obstruction.

Primary Theorems 2.12-2.13 force two eigenvalues at the optimum; rank-one spectral projection is a short uniqueness route. A 2023 primary-publication search lead explicitly reports solving the two-eigenvalue conjecture (doi:10.1016/j.amc.2022.127615); body not accessed because ScienceDirect is prohibited. No novelty or complete prior-proof-body clearance claimed.

All maximizing vectors deterministic is stronger than existence of a corner optimizer, especially under coincident channels/tied objectives. Need exact objective and tie convention from the model; numerical corner plots cannot establish uniqueness or convexity. No domain-degeneracy credit.

Literal includes k=0; a nonempty edgeless graph cannot have a partition into zero forests under positive-colour threshold convention. This is an endpoint correction only; for k>=1 balancing while preserving forests remains a genuine all-m equitable partition problem.

Conjecture 6.1 is monotonicity along implicit boundary branches for all k,q, with q=2 exception. Derivatives involve both root dependence and log-theta normalization; monotonicity of an auxiliary K is insufficient for alpha=log K/log theta. No uniform sign identity established.

Primary Phi_k(d) uses powers of degree-k binary forms (quadratic title is too narrow). Conjecture 5.4 asks bounded error for all k,d; asymptotic construction bounds do not give a uniform additive lower bound.

Source Section 3/Table 2 reports h(24)=234 and H(24)=236, explicitly refuting H=h; Sections 2-3 give bounded covering enumeration and CRT interpretation. This is public computation, not a new certificate here; ancillary exhaustive search not independently replayed.

Conjecture 3.2 is strict doubling for every k>=3. Kanold H<=2^k does not compare adjacent maxima; parity and CRT covering extensions yield only weaker comparisons. Finite known values do not certify the recurrence.

Primary Conjecture 1.10 uses F-matrix/f-vector data, not an undifferentiated F-polynomial equality. Theorem 1.11 covers finite type and rank two; unrestricted cluster type requires injectivity beyond these cases and cannot follow from that theorem alone.

Conjecture 6.1 reduces via R(4,5)=25 and the public 24-vertex check to n=21,22,23. This is genuinely finite, but exhaustive K4-free alpha<=4 Ramsey certification is substantial; no complete classification or SAT unsat proof is available in this lane.

Primary Table 6 provides actual entries omitted from literal; universal Hall-ratio bounds require all induced subgraphs. Pattern LP domination could give finite certificates, but paper reports manageable calculations only for small depth/degree; none supplied for every requested entry here.

Kantor growth claim needs a specified varying n,p regime and equivalence action. Known inequivalent semifield/MRD constructions are prior families; no uniform superpolynomial lower count for the literal quantifiers extracted from a fixed parameter statement.
